editorial:
Imagine hearing the same crazy family story your entire life, only to realize it sounds like something straight out of a movie. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow a director who is digging into a wild tale told by her grandmother, Alice. The story claims that when Alice was a little girl, a massive hurricane actually picked her up and flew her through the air, just like in The Wizard of Oz. It is a quirky, personal journey that feels like sitting in a living room listening to an elderly relative tell a tall tale, making the whole experience feel warm and intimate.

What really works is how the film handles the line between truth and imagination. You will love how it pieces together memory and family history, though the slow pace might feel a bit too quiet for some of you. If you enjoy deep dives into family secrets and odd memories, you should definitely check this out. Since it is a visual exploration, I suggest streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small details, or you could rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night at home.
endingExplained: The movie ends by showing that it does not really matter if the hurricane story was 100 percent true. The director realizes that the story exists because it helped her grandmother shape her own identity and survive hard times. Instead of finding a scientific proof, the film wraps up by embracing the magic of family lore. It concludes that the act of storytelling is more important than the actual facts of the event.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family mysteries and personal stories.
